title.narrative: SEPA, Environmental Governance in the Mining Sector, 2022-2026

description.narrative:
Cooperation between Swedish Environmental Protection Agency, SMHI and SGU, and Zambian authorities and organisations on environmental governance and implementation of Zambias National Adaptation Plan, with focus on mining.
The Swedish Environmental Protection Agency (SEPA) and partners (Swedish Geological Survey, SGU, Swedish Meteorological and Hydrological Institute, SMHI) have presented a proposal for an intervention focusing on integrating environment, climate and human rights to mining governance. The partners will cooperate closely with partners in Zambia, including the United Nations Development Programme in Zambia, UNDP Zambia, Diakonia, Action Aid Zambia, Transparency International Zambia and Global Water Partnership., GWP. The Ministry of Green Economy and Environment (MoGEE) will together with the Zambian Environmental Management Agency, ZEMA, be SEPAs main counterpart in the Zambian administration. SEPA and the project team will also engage with the Ministry of Mines and Minerals Development, industry organisations like Zambia Chamber of Mines, and other industry representatives.SEPA, SMHI and SGU are Swedish authorities, representing the Swedish public administration model, and are all engaged in development cooperation with support from Sida. SEPA is an active member in the Public Agency Hub and a central assessment of SEPA has been undertaken.UNDP globally and UNDP Zambia already cooperates with SEPA within the global Environmental Governance Programme (EGP) since 2014 which focus on integrating environment and human Rights into the governance of the mining sector. Diakonia in Zambia works to strengthen accountability in communities in natural resource rich areas.The proposed programme builds on earlier cooperation and experiences, including SEPA collaboration with UNDP, SMHI International Training Programmes (ITPs) on climate change, SGU ITPs on mine water and mine waste management, and Diakonia's activities in Zambia. The programme will address the following areas:-licensing and permitting process of large scale mining operations as well as awareness raising-knowledge generation and strategic planning related to climate change issues connected to mining-enhancement of the national discourse on sustainable mining by gathering strategic actors to highlight and amass joint pressure on certain "hot topics" related to the Zambian mining sector -provide channels for Zambian actors within the mining value chain to access and interact with regional and global platforms with similar aims as the programmeThe draft agreement follows the agreed Sida templates for General and Specific Conditions for Grants to Swedish Governmental Authorities.

Samarbete med Naturvårdsverket , SMHI och SGU med zambiska myndigheter och organisationer om hållbar förvaltning av gruvsektorn samt genomförande av Zambias klimatanpassningsplan med fokus på gruvdrift,

The Strengthening Zambian Mining Governance in the Nexus of Environment, Human Rights, and Climate (ZAMNEX) programme aims to promote sustainability in Zambias mining sector by integrating environmental protection, human rights, and climate change considerations into governance frameworks.
The programme aims to deliver strategic outputs that contribute to long-term, institutionalized change. This is achieved through capacity building, technical collaboration, and support for national policy dialogue.
ZAMNEX focuses on three core target areas:
Component 1: Strengthening mine closure planning To strengthen the procedures and processes in selected steps of the mining licensing cycle. SGU is co-leading the component together with SEPA. Outcome: Project stakeholders have enhanced their knowledge, participation, and engagement regarding mine closure procedures.
Component 2: Advancing Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) practices To enable interactions between strategic actors and highlight certain identified hot topics related to the Zambian mining sector. The component will also provide coordination opportunities between government bodies currently holding responsibilities governing the mining sector. The CSR network will co-lead this component with SEPA. Outcome: Increased awareness within relevant stakeholders about CSR in Zambia. Outcome: CSR recommendations coming out from the platform has been accepted and integrated within key stakeholders.
Component 3: Developing early warning and impact-based warning systems related to mining activities Providing a systemic understanding of links between climate change. SMHI is co-leading this together with SEPA. Outcome: Reliable and timely warnings adapted to the artisanal and big entity mining actors are distributed Outcome: Target actors increase actions based on information and vulnerability

title.narrative: SEPA, Environmental Governance in the Mining Sector
SEPA, Environmental Governance in the Mining Sector

description.narrative:
During 2025, ZAMNEX achieved several important institutional and policy-level results that contribute to improved governance of Zambia's mining sector and support the sustainable management of natural resources and ecosystems.
One key result was continued progress towards the development of Zambia's first Mine Closure Plan Guideline (ZAMNEX annual report 2025, p. 68). The guideline addresses environmental rehabilitation, biodiversity restoration, mine waste management and sustainable post-mining land use. An important actor-level change is that the Ministry of Mines and Minerals Development and the Minerals Regulation Commission have assumed ownership of the process and integrated its development into their ongoing efforts to strengthen mining governance (ZAMNEX annual report 2025, p. 6). This demonstrates increased institutional commitment and leadership by government actors, while ZAMNEX increasingly plays a technical support role.
A second important result was advancement of the National CSR Guiding Framework for Zambia (ZAMNEX annual report 2025, p. 910). During the reporting period, the CSR platform expanded significantly, growing by 440 per cent in terms of participating individuals and institutions. The platform now includes representatives from government, the mining industry, traditional communities, civil society and academia (ZAMNEX annual report 2025, p. 910). This represents a positive change in stakeholder engagement and collaboration, with key actors increasingly participating in structured dialogue on social and environmental governance issues in the mining sector.
A third result was progress towards establishing an Impact-Based Early Warning System for mining-affected areas (ZAMNEX annual report 2025, p. 1113). The programme facilitated collaboration between technical agencies, local stakeholders and mining communities to improve climate risk management and preparedness. This contributes to increased institutional capacity to manage environmental and climate-related risks affecting both ecosystems and communities.
The programme also demonstrates an evidence-based approach. Development of the Mine Closure Plan Guideline has been informed by international benchmarking, expert reviews and field-based studies, while the ongoing case study in North-Western Province is generating local evidence to inform future policy recommendations (ZAMNEX annual report 2025, p. 68). Similarly, development of the Impact-Based Early Warning System combines technical climate analysis with stakeholder consultations and field missions (ZAMNEX annual report 2025, p. 1113).
Progress on gender equality has been made, although challenges remain in achieving balanced participation. Constraints include the limited pool of qualified experts in specialised fields and the ministry-led nomination process, which supports ownership but can restrict gender balance. To address this, ZAMNEX has engaged strategic partners such as civil society organisations, SADC Women in Mining and the Association for Zambian Women in Mining, ensuring that gender perspectives and the voices of women miners are reflected in programme activities. During 2025, gender considerations have primarily been integrated through expert reviews of key frameworks and through inclusive fieldwork practices, including representation of vulnerable groups and the use of gender-competent experts (ZAMNEX annual report 2025, p. 13-14).
Overall, the results achieved during 2025 demonstrate progress towards strengthened environmental governance of Zambia's mining sector and contribute to the strategy objective of strengthened management and sustainable use of natural resources and ecosystems, including biodiversity.
